 ======================================================
 Appearance :
 For the Petitioner/s : Mr.Krishna Pd. Singh, Sr.Adv
 Mrs.Meena Singh, Advocate
 For the Opposite Party/s : Mr.Nityanand Tiwary, App
 ======================================================
 Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Bibek Chaudhuri
 Oral Order
1. The Opposite Party No. 2 is the legally married wife of the Petitioner No. 1, Gorelal Yadav.
2. The instant Criminal Miscellaneous as against the Petitioner No. 1 was dismissed as withdrawn.

3. The Petitioner Nos. 2 and 3 are father-in-law and mother-in-law of the Opposite Party No. 2.
4.

On the basis of a Court complaint submitted by the Opposite Party No. 2, the learned Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Nawada took cognizance of offence upon initial inquiry under Section 200 of the Cr.P.C, under Section 498A of the IPC and Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.23564 of 2016(12) dt.15-07-2024 Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act against the petitioner/husband,
father-in-law and mother-in-law of the Opposite Party No. 2.
5.

The Petitioners have approached this Court for quashing of the criminal proceeding with regard to Nawada P. S. Case No. 419 of 2014 filed by the Opposite Party No. 2 against the Petitioner Nos. 2 and 3.

sentences.text: I have carefully perused the petition of complaint.

7. In the petition of complaint, there is a vague and ambiguous allegation that after marriage of the Opposite Party No. 2, her husband, mother-in-law, father-in-law and brother-in- law did not like the bridal gifts presented to her at the time of marriage by her father and they started demanding for a motorcycle.
Apart from this ambiguous allegation, all specific allegation was against the husband of the Opposite Party No. 2.
The petitioner even did not state any date and time when her mother-in-law and father-in-law demanded a motorcycle from her father.
8. Learned Advocate for the Opposite Party No. 2 submits that the husband of the Opposite Party No. 2 became the Inspector of Excise and he has been residing elsewhere.
He neglects to maintain his wife.

Therefore, unless and until the Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.23564 of 2016(12)
dt.15-07-2024 Petitioner Nos. 2 and 3 are roped in the instant criminal proceeding, the Opposite Party No. 2 will not be able to get any maintenance.

9. The submission made by the learned Advocate on behalf of the Opposite Party No. 2 is not a ground for carrying out a proceeding under Section 498A of the IPC read with Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

10. In such view of the matter, I am not in a position to accept the submission made by the learned Advocate for the Opposite Party No. 2.
11.

Since there is no material of offence under Section 498A of the IPC or Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act made out against the Petitioner Nos. 2 and 3, the criminal proceeding against the Petitioner Nos. 2 and 3 is quashed under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C.
12.
The instant Cr. Misc. Case is, accordingly, allowed, on contest.
13. However, there shall be no order as to costs.

(Bibek Chaudhuri, J) uttam/-
